results.name: single_example_yes_gap
results.description: Yes-rate on non-member targets for one-example sets minus that for sets of 2-4 examples; observed above null means humans generalise from a single example more broadly (relative to larger sets) than the size principle predicts, below means less.
results.code:
# name: single_example_yes_gap
# description: Yes-rate on non-member targets for one-example sets minus that for sets of 2-4 examples; observed above null means humans generalise from a single example more broadly (relative to larger sets) than the size principle predicts, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()[:, None].astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    member = np.any(valid & (ex == t), axis=1)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    a = (~member) & (n == 1); b = (~member) & (n >= 2)
    if not a.any() or not b.any(): return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: first_vs_last_example_proximity
results.description: Among non-member targets of multi-example sets, corr(rating, -|target - first shown example|) minus corr(rating, -|target - last shown example|); nonzero observed vs a near-zero null means order of presentation matters (primacy if positive, recency if negative), which the order-invariant model cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: first_vs_last_example_proximity
# description: Among non-member targets of multi-example sets, corr(rating, -|target - first shown example|) minus corr(rating, -|target - last shown example|); nonzero observed vs a near-zero null means order of presentation matters (primacy if positive, recency if negative), which the order-invariant model cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()[:, None].astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    member = np.any(valid & (ex == t), axis=1)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    m = (~member) & (n >= 2)
    if m.sum() < 3: return 0.0
    first = ex[m, 0]
    last = ex[m][np.arange(m.sum()), n[m] - 1]
    tt = t[m, 0]; y = r[m]
    d1 = -np.abs(tt - first); d2 = -np.abs(tt - last)
    if y.std() == 0 or d1.std() == 0 or d2.std() == 0: return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(d1, y)[0, 1] - np.corrcoef(d2, y)[0, 1])

results.name: far_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate on non-member targets lying more than 20 from every example; observed above null means humans say yes to remote numbers more than the model (unmodelled response noise/broad generalisation), below means less.
results.code:
# name: far_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate on non-member targets lying more than 20 from every example; observed above null means humans say yes to remote numbers more than the model (unmodelled response noise/broad generalisation), below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()[:, None].astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    member = np.any(valid & (ex == t), axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.where(valid, np.abs(ex - t), np.nan), axis=1)
    m = (~member) & (dist > 20)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: distance_gradient_corr
results.description: Correlation between rating and log(1 + distance to nearest example) among non-member targets; observed more negative than null means humans show a steeper graded numeric-proximity falloff than the model's interval hypotheses give, less negative means flatter.
results.code:
# name: distance_gradient_corr
# description: Correlation between rating and log(1 + distance to nearest example) among non-member targets; observed more negative than null means humans show a steeper graded numeric-proximity falloff than the model's interval hypotheses give, less negative means flatter.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()[:, None].astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    member = np.any(valid & (ex == t), axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.where(valid, np.abs(ex - t), np.nan), axis=1)
    m = ~member
    x = np.log1p(dist[m]); y = r[m]
    if x.std() == 0 or y.std() == 0: return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(x, y)[0, 1])

results.name: member_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate on trials whose target is one of the shown examples; observed below null means the model over-predicts yes for examples (humans lapse/say no to shown members far more than the model allows).

# name: member_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate on trials whose target is one of the shown examples; observed below null means the model over-predicts yes for examples (humans lapse/say no to shown members far more than the model allows).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()[:, None].astype(float)

results.name: parity_match_effect
results.description: Among non-member targets, yes-rate when target parity matches all examples minus when it does not; observed above null means humans weight parity similarity more than the model's odd/even rules produce, below means less.
results.code:
# name: parity_match_effect
# description: Among non-member targets, yes-rate when target parity matches all examples minus when it does not; observed above null means humans weight parity similarity more than the model's odd/even rules produce, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()[:, None].astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    member = np.any(valid & (ex == t), axis=1)
    par = np.all(~valid | (np.mod(ex, 2) == np.mod(t, 2)), axis=1)
    a = (~member) & par; b = (~member) & ~par
    if not a.any() or not b.any(): return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: trial_block_yes_variance
results.description: Variance of the yes-rate across consecutive blocks of 50 trial_index positions (pooled over participants); observed above null means responding drifts over the session in a way the stationary model cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: trial_block_yes_variance
# description: Variance of the yes-rate across consecutive blocks of 50 trial_index positions (pooled over participants); observed above null means responding drifts over the session in a way the stationary model cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    b = (df["trial_index"].astype(int).to_numpy() // 50)
    s = pd.Series(r).groupby(b).mean()
    return float(s.var(ddof=0)) if len(s) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: last_digit_match_effect
results.description: Among non-member targets, yes-rate when the target shares its last digit with at least one example minus when it shares with none; observed above null means humans use partial digit similarity more than the model's all-examples 'ends in d' rules allow, below means less.
results.code:
# name: last_digit_match_effect
# description: Among non-member targets, yes-rate when the target shares its last digit with at least one example minus when it shares with none; observed above null means humans use partial digit similarity more than the model's all-examples 'ends in d' rules allow, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()[:, None].astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    member = np.any(valid & (ex == t), axis=1)
    dm = np.any(valid & (np.mod(ex, 10) == np.mod(t, 10)), axis=1)
    a = (~member) & dm; b = (~member) & ~dm
    if not a.any() or not b.any(): return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
